blindSummary:
This state/province carries three sub-national negatives absent elsewhere in the country: the education minister ordered the 2019 transgender-pupils guidance withdrawn from the regional education body's website in September 2025 after a supreme-court ruling on biological sex, calling it unlawful and flawed and a product of activist campaigning; the justice minister's attempt to include transgender people as a protected group in hate-crime sentencing reform was stalled (reported obstruction by the main unionist party); and an LGBTQ monitoring organisation records a pattern of paramilitary-flavoured anti-LGB&T violence — including a pipe bomb thrown through the home of a trans woman described by the police force as a 'sectarian hate crime', a 2019 city-centre assault hospitalising a gay man, and an average of ~290 anti-LGB&T incidents per year (2013–2017) with rising transgender-identity strand counts to September 2025.

Counter-balancing: the police and statistics bodies track a separate 'transgender identity' category (unlike in most other parts of the country), evidencing institutional recognition; the health minister publicly defended a gender-identity service funding uplift of more than three-quarters of a million local-currency units against unionist criticism, showing the executive is split rather than uniformly hostile. No criminal ban on expression or police-enforced facility prohibition exists — the risk mechanism is the national equality-watchdog facility code (service refusal by staff) plus street-level violence.
blindSourceSummaries: A national broadcaster (8 September 2025): the regional education body's 2019 guidance on supporting transgender pupils is withdrawn from its website after a supreme-court ruling on biological sex; the education minister requested the withdrawal, said the guidance did not reflect departmental policy and was inconsistent with local law, and called it a product of activist campaigning; opposition parties press for reinstatement and disclosure of the legal advice.

A national broadcaster: the justice minister's attempt to add transgender people as a protected group in hate-crime sentencing reform is being stalled, with the main unionist party reported to be blocking the measure.

A newspaper: an exploding pipe bomb was thrown through the window of the home of a 27-year-old trans woman while she watched television; the police force treated it as a hate crime with sectarian framing and she was forced to move out.

An LGBTQ monitoring organisation's hate-crime page: an average of about 290 reported anti-LGB&T incidents and crimes per year (2013–2017), reporting stagnant, and quarterly series running back to 2004/05 including a separate transgender-identity strand.

A national broadcaster: the health minister publicly defends an uplift of more than three-quarters of a million (local currency) for gender-identity health services against unionist criticism, evidencing a divided executive rather than uniform hostility.
blindTangential: The violence record mixes anti-gay and anti-trans incidents (the 2019 city-centre assault was anti-gay; the ~290/year series counts anti-LGB&T broadly) — the trans strand is smaller but separately tracked and rising.
blindLocalsOnly: The withdrawn school guidance bore on trans pupils in resident families; the stalled protected-group reform concerns sentencing for offences against residents — a visitor encounters both as climate and policing-culture signals rather than direct machinery.
